name: severally-mcp

tools.name: consult_start
tools.description:
Start a consultation with another agent (or several, via targets). Returns a job_id (or a group_id for several) at once; the work runs in the background.

target: which consultant to ask. This machine can reach (name: CLI, model):
          (none -- no consultant CLI is installed)
        Pass the word the user used: a name, a CLI ("codex", "agy"), a vendor or a model ("claude opus"). One
        that fits several, unresolved by the operator's ranking, tier and version, is refused with the
        candidates (target_ambiguous); one not listed is refused (target_unavailable). Your own CLI on a fresh
        session is a valid consultant, marked same lineage.
targets: several consultants, the same question (not with target, no duplicates); targets: ["all"] is every
        consultant listed above. Every member gets the byte-identical brief (a follow-up adds its own earlier
        rounds) and one group_id, for consult_get and consult_cancel. A fan-out over the concurrency cap is
        refused before any member starts.
followup_to: the job_id of the answer to continue, or a group_id to ask every member of that fan-out again
        (each on its own chain; a member that cannot take one is skipped and listed). A follow-up needs only
        followup_to and question: everything else is the earlier round's unless you pass it, and a value you pass,
        even empty, replaces it. Its files are copied again as they are now, with any expose_paths you add;
        context.expose_from_parent: false keeps them back. A follow-up cannot change the consultant.
mode: optional, read from context when left out: no proposal is explore, a proposal is review, a proposal with
        counterpoints is debate. review and debate need context.proposal (your plan and its reasoning); debate
        also needs context.counterpoints (the other side's claims); explore refuses a proposal on round 1.
context: optional when the question supplies the needed information. For code questions, attach files or a diff.
        The consultant starts in an empty working directory and is not told where your repository is. Supply
        additional material as facts, artifacts (not a file here: test output, a log), expose_paths (absolute
        paths, copied read-only under ./workspace; a git work tree's
        directory copies the files git lists; at most 20 entries, 500 files, 5 MB; symlinks and protected files
        are skipped; text is credential-masked like the brief), expose_diff: { repo, base? } (the diff in the
        brief, its files under ./workspace/repo/).
network: "on" (default) or "off" (no web search or browsing for any consultant this round). Credential and
        history paths are refused either way where the CLI can enforce it; each answer's `boundary` says what held.
caller, caller_model: the CLI and model you run on (self-declared), for the same-vendor caveat and the record.
initiator: "user" when the user asked for this; leave it out when you started it yourself.
prediction: { expected, worry }, kept and never sent; it can only be written here, before the answer.
Model, permissions, rounds, timeout and size caps are fixed by this server.

expected.description: the bottom line you expect to come back

worry.description: the one thing you are most worried about, in a sentence

tools.name: consult_get
tools.description: Fetch a consultation's state or answer. It waits up to 45000 ms (under this client's tool-call timeout) for it to finish; wait_ms sets another wait, 0 answers at once. While waiting it sends a progress notification every 15 s when asked; a cancelled call stops waiting. Most take one to ten minutes: call again while status is running. completed carries the structured answer; failed carries failure.kind (timeout, auth, usage_limit, rate_limited, model_unavailable, invalid_output, cli_error, spawn_error, interrupted), meaning no advice was obtained -- not the same as advice with thin evidence (quality.evidence_basis, quality.caveat). group_id fetches a fan-out: each member's status, failure and job_id, and `comparison.by_target` with each actual model, stance, summary and finding (id and grounds), cut where `truncated` says so. ids: ["f2", "u1"] with a job_id returns just those points, whole, with their grounds and your verdict (`recorded`). A finished consultation names its brief rather than repeating it; detail: "full" returns the brief and the question whole; a fan-out member's whole answer is consult_get({ job_id }). Before your final report, check one point that could change the decision, then save the outcome with consult_record({ job_id, entries: [{ id, verdict, note, effect }] }). Record an actual local check as confirmed or not_applicable; a point only read stays unverified, and a check you cannot run is unverifiable. Read the grounds already shown; do not fetch them again when whole. For a fan-out fetch deciding points with ids when their grounds or details are missing or shortened, or a member's job_id for its whole answer. Record checked points in one records batch. Report each consultant's stance and actual model, your check, recommendation and unchecked points.

ids.description: with job_id: return only these points of the finished answer (f1, u1, c1 ...), each whole with its grounds and, under `recorded`, the verdict you wrote

tools.name: consult_cancel
tools.description: Stop a running consultation and kill the consultant process and everything it spawned. Pass group_id instead of job_id to stop every consultant in a fan-out. One another severally server runs is asked to stop, and that server stops it within a second.

tools.name: consult_record
tools.description: Write your verdict on points of an answer after checking them: ids f1 ... (findings), u1 ... (unknowns), c1 ... (next_checks). verdict is what checking showed -- confirmed (holds here), not_applicable (true in general, not here), unverifiable, unverified (not checked yet; say why in effect) -- not whether you adopted it. effect is what it changed about your decision, note the evidence. A follow-up shows the consultant each verdict and effect (credential-masked), never the note. The same id again replaces the entry. Saved beside the answer in ~/.severally/history, so a job from an earlier session can be recorded against; the server never infers a verdict. Answers with counts; consult_get reads the entries back. reflection records what the answer added over your consult_start prediction. records: [{ job_id, entries, reflection? }, ...] records every member of a fan-out in one call; all are checked first and nothing is written if any job or id is wrong. A job whose write fails is listed under results with its error.

id.description: f1, u1, c1 ... from the result

effect.description: what it changed, or why it is unverified

delta.description: what the answer added over what you expected ("nothing new" counts)

records.description: one per fan-out member, instead of job_id/entries/reflection

id.description: f1, u1, c1 ... from the result

effect.description: what it changed, or why it is unverified

delta.description: what the answer added over what you expected ("nothing new" counts)

tools.name: consult_export
tools.description: Render one consultation (chain_id) or fan-out (group_id) as Markdown: the brief as sent, each answer as it came back, and the verdicts on each point, unchecked ones marked. Nothing is summarised or scored. The text is returned, not written: put it beside the code the decision is about. Reads the history, so an earlier session's consultation can be exported.

tools.name: consult_list
tools.description: Recent consultations, earlier sessions' too (this_session is false), newest first, with their ids, status, summary and verdicts; and usage_totals, the tokens (and cost) each consultant reported this session, retries included. A figure a CLI does not report is named under not_reported, not counted as zero.

instructions:
severally lets you get a genuinely independent opinion from another coding agent:
Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity or OpenCode, each on the models the operator set up as consultants.
Each consultation runs in a fresh child session of that CLI: it can read files and search and browse the web;
it cannot edit files, change anything on the system (Codex may run read-only commands), load MCP tools, start
other agents or consult anyone else. The server sends the brief and explicitly exposed files without your
conversation history; the CLI may also read other files within its permission boundary.

Use it for decisions that deserve a second mind: an architectural or irreversible choice, two options that
look genuinely close, or an investigation that has stalled. Do not use it for routine edits.

Flow: consult_start -> consult_get until done -> check one decision-changing point locally -> consult_record
with the check and its effect -> report to the user. Use consult_cancel to stop a consultation.
Budget is 1 initial round plus at most 4 follow-ups per chain, and follow-ups should be
spent only on the specific points where you and the consultant actually diverge. Agreement is not evidence:
check the grounds behind a point before you adopt it, and record what you adopted, rejected or held, and why.
